title: Build a reverse-mode autodiff engine
brief: Implement a tape-based Tensor with vector-Jacobian products for the ops an MLP needs, then use it to compute an MLP's loss and every gradient in one backward pass.
hints: Every op's _backward_fn should use += on a child's .grad, never =, since a tensor used more than once must accumulate contributions from every place it was used.

__add__ and __mul__ must handle numpy broadcasting (a bias vector added to a batch of rows): call the provided _unbroadcast(out.grad_or_product, operand.value.shape) before accumulating into that operand's .grad.

backward()'s topological sort is a DFS over _children that appends a node to the order only after all of its children have been appended, then walks that order in reverse; this is the standard pattern and handles a diamond-shaped graph correctly as long as a visited set prevents revisiting a shared ancestor.

softmax_cross_entropy: compute probs with a numerically stable softmax, then the gradient with respect to the logits is (probs - one_hot(labels)) / n, derived in the lesson by combining the softmax Jacobian with cross-entropy's gradient.
